topic: Definitions of Sine, Cosine and Other Trigonometric Functions
title: How High Is the Valve? Sine Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Turn a bicycle wheel slowly and follow the valve. It rises, it falls, it swings left and right. For any angle the wheel turns, how high is the valve? That height has a name: sine. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we define sine, cosine and the four other trigonometric functions on the unit circle.

You will see P(a, b) on the unit circle with cos x as its x coordinate (blue) and sin x as its y coordinate (coral), watch both values change live as x counts up to 2π, and find exactly where sine and cosine are zero. We compare sine and cosine side by side, build tan, cot, sec and cosec from them with live values (and see tan blow up at π/2), find all six functions at π/4 in a worked example, fix the cosec trap, and solve an original JEE Main pattern question. Two pause-and-think questions, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 How high is the valve?
0:27 Definition: cos x and sin x on the unit circle
0:55 Live values from 0 to 2π
1:22 Where are sine and cosine zero?
2:01 Cosine vs sine
2:36 tan, cot, sec and cosec
3:27 Worked example: all six at π/4
4:02 Exam trap: cosec is not sine inverse
4:16 Where it is asked
4:26 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:03 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 28): Signs in Different Quadrants. The valve can be above or below the hub, left or right: which signs do sine and cosine take?
